taxonomy.note: Current Kew recognizes subsp. hallii and subsp. filipes; B009 remains species-level pending a need for subspecies-level field instruction.

evidence: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum hallii, lists Texas as native, and recognizes subsp. hallii and subsp. filipes.
Hagenbuch & Lemke explicitly record multiple Hays County specimens.
The same appendix records Blanco County (Lackey 777, SWT).
The same appendix records Val Verde County (Labus 301, 326, 352, SWT).
target_zone_range.guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for a short blue-gray bunch: mostly basal stiff glaucous leaves and a relatively small open pyramidal panicle whose branches are stiff and ascending.
diagnostic_traits: glaucous internodes and stiff glaucous leaves
open pyramidal panicle only about 6–20 cm
primary panicle branches stiff and ascending

confusers.separator: Switchgrass is much taller and rhizomatous with a much larger diffuse panicle.
Witchgrass is annual and strongly hairy with a huge lax panicle; Hall's is perennial, glaucous and stiffer.

installation_guardrail: Do not install until Calvin explicitly approves B009 pass taxa.
